newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi gasoline spill is "major" -Coast Guard.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi gasoline spill is "major" -Coast Guard.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard Marine Safety Office in Memphis, Tennessee said Thursday that a "major spill" occurred when approximately 15,000 gallons of gasoline was spilled into the Mississippi River when a barge ran aground Wednesday night.
Traffic has been stopped on a 13-mile stretch of the river, which usually sees heavy flows.

The M/V Shirley L. Stapp was the lead barge in a chain of four being towed northbound when it ran aground about 18 miles downstream of Memphis at about 1900 CST on Wednesday, the Coast Guard said Thursday.
The cause of the grounding was under investigation, the Coast Guard said in a statement.

The Coast Guard is bringing specialized equipment to the area and is working with state officials to off-load remaining gasoline from the barge, according to Lt. Byron Black of the Coast Guard Marine Safety Office in Memphis.

"The equipment is expected to appear this evening or tomorrow morning and we are looking at the possibility of having a limited opening of the river until we begin lightering (off-loading) operations," said Black.
"It is like an interstate being closed with no way out," said Black.
There were no people evacuated in this sparsely populated area, the Coast Guard said.

The main danger is the possibility of the flammable vapors catching fire and breathing dangerous fumes, said Black. However, gasoline evaporates much easier than other, heavier oil products, Black added.
